scope: Two new authored questions, two repetitions, shared v1 public corpus. Numbered exact source excerpts and deterministic read-reference routing; not a held-out quality comparison or production retrieval evaluation.
provenance: Real server run records exported through the operator results page. Source quotes are deterministically recovered by evidenceId from the frozen protocol; model does not author quotes. No failed attempt is replaced. No original provider response bodies retained.
limitations: New authored questions with the same public corpus; not a held-out quality evaluation.
Two repetitions cannot establish general stability. Different goals and protocol from v1 prevent causal claims about an improvement.
Read-reference routing is a deterministic product rule based only on visible explicit memory, not evidence that the model learned the preference.

recommendations.reason: Foundational CLT for convex sets; directly connects convexity to Gaussian marginals and separates the geometric assumption from the quantitative conclusion.
recommendations.quote: We argue that convexity - and perhaps geometry in general - may replace the role of independence in certain aspects of the phenomenon represented by the central limit theorem.
recommendations.title: A Central Limit Theorem for Convex Sets

recommendations.reason: Provides Poincare-type inequalities on convex bodies and generalizes the CLT for convex bodies to some non-convex domains, clarifying which geometric assumptions drive Gaussian behavior.
recommendations.quote: In particular, we generalize the central limit theorem for convex bodies to a class of non-convex domains, including the unit balls of L_p-spaces in R^n for 0 < p < 1.
recommendations.title: Poincare Inequalities and Moment Maps

recommendations.reason: Links improved KLS isoperimetric bounds to thin-shell and concentration consequences, useful for separating isoperimetric assumptions from Gaussian-type conclusions.
recommendations.quote: Improving the current best lower bound of the isoperimetric coefficient in the KLS conjecture has many implications, including improvements of the current best bounds in Bourgain's slicing conjecture and in the thin-shell conjecture, better concentration inequalities for Lipschitz functions of log-concave measures and better mixing time bounds for MCMC sampling algorithms on log-concave measures.
recommendations.title: An Almost Constant Lower Bound of the Isoperimetric Coefficient in the KLS Conjecture

recommendations.reason: Gives quantitative polylogarithmic bounds for Bourgain slicing and KLS, directly relevant to thin-shell estimates and their quantitative relation to Gaussian approximation.
recommendations.quote: We prove that the Bourgain slicing conjecture and the Kannan-Lovász-Simonovits (KLS) isoperimetric conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^n$ hold true up to a factor of $\sqrt{\log n}$.
recommendations.title: Logarithmic bounds for isoperimetry and slices of convex sets

recommendations.reason: Survey of KLS origins, consequences and techniques, helpful for organizing assumptions and quantitative conclusions across geometry, probability and algorithms.
recommendations.quote: Here we survey the origin and consequences of the conjecture (in geometry, probability, information theory and algorithms) as well as recent progress resulting in the current best bounds.
recommendations.title: The Kannan-Lov\'asz-Simonovits Conjecture

recommendations.reason: Directly extends finite-blocklength joint source-channel coding, giving the non-asymptotic bound with distortion-exceedance probability epsilon, which is the probability criterion the goal asks about.
recommendations.quote: A joint source-channel code maps a block of $k$ source symbols onto a length$-n$ channel codeword, and the fidelity of reproduction at the receiver end is measured by the probability $\epsilon$ that the distortion exceeds a given threshold $d$.
recommendations.title: Lossy joint source-channel coding in the finite blocklength regime

recommendations.reason: Treats lossy source coding with side information at both encoder and decoder, clarifying who knows what and giving second-order/non-asymptotic bounds.
recommendations.quote: This paper characterizes the second-order coding rates for lossy source coding with side information available at both the encoder and the decoder.
recommendations.title: Second-Order Coding Rates for Conditional Rate-Distortion

recommendations.reason: Provides tight fixed-blocklength achievability and converse bounds in terms of probability epsilon that distortion exceeds d, useful for the probability criterion.
recommendations.quote: This paper studies the minimum achievable source coding rate as a function of blocklength $n$ and probability $\epsilon$ that the distortion exceeds a given level $d$.
recommendations.title: Fixed-length lossy compression in the finite blocklength regime

recommendations.reason: Gives non-asymptotic lossy source coding bounds with probability of exceeding distortion d no greater than epsilon, relevant to the probability criterion.
recommendations.quote: This paper considers lossy source coding of $n$-dimensional memoryless sources and shows an explicit approximation to the minimum source coding rate required to sustain the probability of exceeding distortion $d$ no greater than $\epsilon$, which is simpler than known dispersion-based approximations.
recommendations.title: Data compression with low distortion and finite blocklength
